topics.topic: How missing provenance principals and transition times are assigned to imported artifact pointers
questions: What facts are assigned to an imported pointer when the source does not supply the newly required publication or withdrawal principal or a required status-change instant?
What withdrawal-time fact does an imported pointer with status `withdrawn` carry?
What published-by and withdrawn-by facts do imported pointers carry when the legacy source has no ActingPrincipal values?
How are the required provenance and transition facts populated for an imported pointer when the source does not carry them?

quotes: A record the import brings in keeps the instants its source holds: a project's created, last-changed and archived instants, a room's added instant, a pointer's published and superseded instants.

written once: the instant it was published and by which principal (M07) — a producer service as its token names it, Kernel for the agent naming its session, or the owner for any owner service; the instant it was superseded; the instant it was withdrawn and by which principal (R0-14).
judgement.divergence: One implementer assigns import-time or importing-owner provenance and transition instants when legacy facts are missing; another preserves missing or unknown values. The owner and any caller reading artifact history notice different pointer facts.
judgement.why: The required facts of imported ArtifactPointers are not defined when the legacy source lacks the newly required provenance or withdrawal instant.

topics.topic: How otherwise identical AuditEntry entities receive distinct identities
questions: What makes two fact-for-fact equal AuditEntries distinct, and who creates that identity?
What distinguishes and names two AuditEntry entities whose listed facts are identical?
What gives two otherwise equal AuditEntry entities distinct identity?

quotes: This state names the concepts Registry needs, the facts each carries in domain words, its identity (`value` or `entity`, `MODEL_IDENTITY_EVIDENCE.md`), who creates, reads and changes it, its status vocabulary and what is written once.

Substitution: two entries with equal facts are two events — two archivings of two projects at the same instant, or an erasure and its re-run — and the log is read in time order as distinct entries (R0-58).
judgement.divergence: One implementer gives every AuditEntry a Registry-minted identifier; another identifies entries only by storage occurrence or position. The owner reading or retaining duplicate audit events, and later contracts that name entries, observe different identity and stability.
judgement.why: AuditEntry is an entity whose equal instances remain distinct, but the texts define neither its identifying fact nor who creates it.

topics.topic: Whether unchanged confirmed actions receive confirmation ids and audit entries
questions: When a confirmed action succeeds as an unchanged no-op, is a confirmation id minted, and is an audit entry created to retain it?
Does a successful but state-preserving repeat such as re-archiving or re-anonymising create an AuditEntry and confirmation id?
When a confirmed action succeeds as an unchanged no-op, is a confirmation id minted and is an AuditEntry written?

judgement.why: This is the same question as P1 about confirmation ids and AuditEntries for confirmed state-preserving or refused actions, and the relevant texts have not changed.

Which actions must state

precedent.why: Whether a confirmed invocation is accepted, refused, treated as a no-op, and consequently emits an audit entry or confirmation id is an operation rule owned by State 2.

topics.topic: Which subject facts AuditEntries use for imports and audit-log erasures
questions: What subject fact does each non-project/customer entry carry, especially the import entry and the audit-erasure entry?
What subject facts do the import entry and the audit-entry-erasure entry carry?
What subject alternatives can an AuditEntry carry for imports and audit-log erasures?

quotes: the import, as one entry whose subject is the migration closure (M10); erasing old entries.
the subject: the project (`project_id`) or the customer (`customer_ref`) changed, by identity only (R0-37) — for a session grant, the session and the project;
judgement.why: The import entry is said to have MigrationClosure as its subject, while the complete subject fact permits only a project, customer, or session-and-project and supplies no subject for audit-log erasure.

topics.topic: Whether project anonymisation is stored explicitly or inferred from retained facts
questions: Is anonymisation represented by a stored Project fact, or inferred from an archived record having only the retained facts?
Is the anonymised mark a persisted Project fact, or must anonymisation be inferred from the absence of the erased facts?

quotes: An anonymised project keeps its id, status and artifact pointers and nothing else.

An anonymised project is a Project with status `archived` and the anonymised mark: it keeps its `project_id`, its status, that mark and its artifact pointers (M05) and nothing else (R0-62) — name, alias, object, customer link, rooms, revision and every instant are gone; when it was archived and when it was anonymised, the audit log says (M09).
judgement.why: State 0 excludes every retained fact beyond id, status and pointers, while State 1 additionally retains an anonymised mark.

topics.topic: Whether project erasure also creates per-session revocation audit entries
questions: When project erasure removes grants from one or more sessions, does Registry write only the project-erasure entry or also one revocation entry for each affected session?
Does anonymising or deleting a project create one project-erasure entry only, or also one revocation entry for every affected session?

quotes: When the owner anonymises or deletes an archived project, it leaves the granted set of every agent session, and a session whose active project it was has none. No session keeps a grant on an erased project.

The actions that write an entry (R0-58): creating, correcting, archiving, anonymising and deleting a project; recording, correcting and erasing a customer; restricting and lifting; ending and resuming a relationship; granting a project to a session and revoking one; the import, as one entry whose subject is the migration closure (M10); erasing old entries.
judgement.divergence: One implementation writes only the project-erasure AuditEntry; another also writes a revocation entry for every session whose grant is automatically removed. The owner reading the audit log notices one entry versus one plus an entry per affected session.
judgement.why: The texts require audit entries for erasure and revocation but do not say whether removals induced by erasure count as separately audited revocations.

topics.topic: Which artifact pointers are included in the agent projection
questions: Which ArtifactPointers does reading the agent projection return?
Which ArtifactPointer records does reading the agent projection include?

quotes: The agent projection: `project_id`, alias, status, rooms, pointers — nothing held as `personal_data` (R0-43, R0-68, R0-82).
every pointer of the project — published, superseded and withdrawn — each with its type, version and status; this is how history is read (R0-02)
judgement.divergence: One implementer includes every published, superseded and withdrawn pointer in the agent projection; another includes only currently published pointers. The agent and Cabinet Kernel notice whether historical pointers are returned.
judgement.why: The projection names pointers without specifying whether it reads the complete history or only current publications.

quotes: missing name or kind refused; recording the same person again makes a second Customer (R0-16)
judgement.why: The recording action refuses only a missing name or kind, so phone, e-mail and language are not required at creation.
